knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# read data
data <- read.csv(
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/sara_data_VM.csv",
  na.strings = "-999"
)
```

```{r}
#comission/omission errors correlated?

cor.test(data$err_com,
         data$err_om,
         method = "spearman",
         exact = FALSE)

```

moderately positive correlation (significant)

```{r}
#are impulsive errors correlated to comission errors??

#total
cor.test(data$imp_err_total,
         data$err_com,
         method = "spearman",
         exact = FALSE)

#on imp erorrs3
cor.test(data$imp_err3,
         data$err_com,
         method = "spearman",
         exact = FALSE)
```

moderately positive correlation (significant) for both

```{r}
cor.test(data$imp_err_total,
         data$err_om,
         method = "spearman",
         exact = FALSE)
```

moderately positive correlation (significant)

```{r}
#comission errors related to attention?
  cor.test(data$err_com,
         data$d_prime,
         method = "spearman",
         exact = FALSE)
```

very strong negative correlation

```{r}
cor.test(data$err_com,
         data$dsm_inatten,
         method = "spearman",
         exact = FALSE)

cor.test(data$err_com,
         data$bis_second,
         method = "spearman",
         exact = FALSE)

```

no correlation.. even if yes, positive

```{r}
#does commission error related to resilience after controlling for impulsivity?
#sel report imp
library(ppcor)

pcor.test(
  x = data$err_com,
  y = data$cdrisc,
  z = data$bis_second,
  method = "spearman"
)
```

```{r}
#same but objective imp
pcor.test(
  x = data$err_com,
  y = data$cdrisc,
  z = data$imp_err_total,
  method = "spearman")
```

That means controlling for impulsivity did not uncover a hidden relationship between comission errors and resilience.

```{r}
#commission error related to resilience after controlling for attention?

pcor.test(
  x = data$err_com,
  y = data$cdrisc,
  z = data$d_prime,
  method = "spearman"
)

```

That means controlling for attention did not uncover a hidden relationship between comission errors and resilience.

```{r}
#How much do self-reported attention, objective attention, and sex each uniquely predict CD-RISC scores?

model <- lm(cdrisc ~ dsm_inatten + d_prime + sex, data = data)

summary(model)

```

```{r}
#Which measures uniquely predict resilience after accounting for the others?

model <- lm(cdrisc ~dsm_inatten + bis_second + d_prime + meanrt + stdrt +sex,data = data
)

summary(model)
```

```{r}
#is this ok?

par(mfrow = c(2,2))
plot(model)
```

```{r}
#interaction
model <- lm(cdrisc ~ dsm_inatten * sex,data = data
)
summary(model)

```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(data, aes(x = d_prime, y = err_com)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(
    x = "Objective Attention (d′)",
    y = "Commission Errors",
    title = "Objective Attention and Commission Errors"
  ) +
  theme_classic()

ggsave(
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/Objective_Attention_Commission_Errors.png",
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600
)
```
